documentsTable.details: Right to work checks, contracts, payslips and contact details.

rules.title: Home Office compliance visits
rules.text: Officers usually check HR records, interview Key Personnel and sometimes speak to sponsored workers.

rules.title: Report changes on time
rules.text: Some changes, such as a worker not starting or leaving early, must be reported within set deadlines.

rules.title: Right to work checks
rules.text: Must be done for every employee before they start. [Read our guide](/right-to-work-checks/)

boxTitle: Want a second pair of eyes before you apply?
boxText: A consultation costs far less than a refused application. We’ll check your case against the current rules and tell you honestly where you stand.

sections.heading: Your sponsor licence compliance duties
sections.text: When you hold a sponsor licence, the Home Office expects you to carry out and keep right to work checks for every employee, keep the records set out in Appendix D for each sponsored worker, report certain changes through the Sponsor Management System, and make sure sponsored workers are doing the job and paid the salary you sponsored them for.

faqs.q: How often does the Home Office visit sponsors?
faqs.a: There’s no fixed schedule. Visits can be before or after a licence is granted, and can be unannounced.
We review your records and processes as a Home Office officer would, and give you a clear report and action list.

faqs.q: Can a downgraded licence be restored?
faqs.a: Usually, by completing the Home Office action plan. We help you through it.
